Playbook.name: QA - Office 365 High Severity - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: This rule surfaces High-severity Microsoft 365 Security and Compliance alerts (o365.audit.Severity == "High"). At JCB these are dominated by Data Loss Prevention policy matches — the SWIFT, payment-card and Jordan-national-ID DLP policies. Because it is a severity-based catch-all, the specific technique depends on the underlying policy; the common case is sensitive data leaving via email or file sharing. Triage question: is this a genuine attempt to move regulated data out (or an account being misused), or authorised business activity / a transfer the DLP policy already blocked?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: For a bank, a High-severity DLP match means regulated data (SWIFT payment data, card PANs, national IDs) was detected leaving the boundary. Confirmed cases are reportable data-loss events and may indicate a compromised or malicious insider account.

Assets.AssetType: Microsoft 365 tenant (JCB) — Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive; Microsoft Purview / Security and Compliance

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: M365 unified audit via Elastic Agent — verified live at JCB (8.1M docs/30d). High-severity events are Security and Compliance alerts: event.code IN ("SecurityComplianceAlerts","SecurityComplianceInsights"), event.provider == "SecurityComplianceCenter", event.action IN ("AlertTriggered","AlertEntityGenerated","AlertUpdated"), o365.audit.Severity == "High" (about 100 events/30d at JCB).

JCB-specific: the affected user/mailbox is in o365.audit.ObjectId as an email (case varies, e.g. jcbank.com.jo vs JCBANK.COM.JO) — match case-insensitively. rule.name is the DLP/alert policy name. o365.audit.Operation is NOT populated at JCB; the action is in event.action. These alert records carry no source.ip. O365 ingest lag is 20-60 min (these compliance alerts can lag more); queries use a 4h window.

Signal.Name: QA - Office 365 High Severity
Signal.Details: An M365 Security and Compliance alert with o365.audit.Severity == "High" for an entity.

Input.name: $entity
Input.description: The affected user / mailbox email the alert is about (o365.audit.ObjectId).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance — identify the policy that matched and whether real sensitive data actually moved (and whether it was blocked), not just that an alert fired.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the High-severity M365 compliance alert reflects a genuine data-loss / account-misuse event, or authorised activity / a transfer the policy already blocked.

Step.name: Identify the alert and the policy that matched
Step.Purpose: Pull the High-severity compliance alert(s) for this entity and read the policy name (rule.name) and the alert lifecycle actions — this tells you what regulated data and channel triggered it.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND o365.audit.Severity == "High" AND TO_LOWER(o365.audit.ObjectId) == TO_LOWER("$entity") | KEEP @timestamp, o365.audit.Severity, rule.name, event.action, event.provider, o365.audit.ObjectId, o365.audit.AlertId | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: rule.name names the DLP/compliance policy (e.g. DLP-JCB-Swift, DLP-JCB-Card, DLP-JCB-Jordan National ID). A regulated-data policy (SWIFT/card/national ID) is the highest-priority. Use the AlertId to open the full alert in the Microsoft Purview / Defender portal for the matched content and the block/allow action.

Step.name: Is this a one-off or a pattern for this entity
Step.Purpose: Summarise this entity's High and Medium compliance alerts across the window — a repeating or escalating pattern (several policies, rising severity) is far more concerning than a single match.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND o365.audit.Severity IN ("High","Medium") AND TO_LOWER(o365.audit.ObjectId) == TO_LOWER("$entity") | STATS alerts = COUNT(*), policies = VALUES(rule.name), severities = VALUES(o365.audit.Severity), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Multiple distinct DLP policies or a burst of matches for one entity suggests deliberate exfiltration or a compromised account, not an accidental single send.

Step.name: Corroborate with the entity's real data-movement activity
Step.Purpose: Look at the affected user's actual exfil-relevant M365 actions in the window — bulk downloads, mailbox access, sends and external sharing — to judge whether real data movement backs the DLP alert.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND (TO_LOWER(user.name) == TO_LOWER("$entity") OR TO_LOWER(user.email) == TO_LOWER("$entity")) | STATS events = COUNT(*), sources = VALUES(source.ip) BY event.action | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: The entity's full action profile in the window (JCB keys the actor as the short user.name and the email user.email; this query matches either). Exfil-relevant actions to weigh: Send / SendAs, MailItemsAccessed, AttachmentAccess, FileDownloadedFromBrowser / FileSyncDownloadedFull, FileUploaded, AnonymousLinkCreated / SharingInvitationCreated. A spike in these, or activity from an unfamiliar source (JCB egress NAT is 94.249.88.0/24; Microsoft service IPs are normal), corroborates real data movement. Little activity, or a Purview outcome showing the transfer was blocked, points to a benign/blocked event.

Node.Condition: A regulated-data DLP policy (SWIFT / card / national ID) matched real outbound content (INV-01) and INV-03 shows corroborating data movement (external send/share, bulk download) that was allowed.
Node.Result: True Positive (Sensitive Data Loss — contain, scope the exposure, notify compliance)

Node.Condition: The activity is authorised business (an approved recipient/process) OR the DLP policy blocked the transfer so no data actually left (proven-blocked).
The policy itself is mis-scoped or over-matching (matching non-sensitive content, or an internal-only flow it should exclude), producing High-severity noise.
Sensitive content plausibly moved but the recipient, the intent or whether it was blocked cannot be confirmed from telemetry alone.

FalsePositive.Definition: Authorised business activity, or a transfer the DLP policy already blocked so no data left.

Indicators.Item: Recipient/process is an approved business counterpart or internal system.
The alert / Purview record shows the action was blocked (BlockAccess) — proven-blocked.
INV-03 shows no unusual external send/share or bulk download for the entity.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the business context or the block in Purview; document; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Regulated data actually left the boundary — a genuine data-loss event, possibly via a compromised or malicious account.

Indicators.Item: Regulated-data policy (SWIFT/card/national ID) matched and the transfer was allowed.
Corroborating external sharing / send / bulk download around the alert time.
Repeating pattern or multiple policies for the same entity.

SOCAction.Item: Contain the account (disable/reset, revoke sessions/tokens) if misuse or compromise is indicated; preserve the Purview alert and matched content.
Scope what data left and to whom; open IR; notify compliance / data-protection.

Misconfiguration.Definition: The DLP/compliance policy is mis-scoped and over-matching, generating High-severity noise.

Indicators.Item: Matches are on non-sensitive or internal-only content.
The same benign flow trips the policy repeatedly for many users.

SOCAction.Item: Refer the policy to the Purview/DLP owners for tuning; document the over-match pattern.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the matched policy and entity (INV-01); open the alert in Purview/Defender via the AlertId to see the content and block/allow action.
If regulated data was allowed to leave, begin containing the account and preserve the evidence.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: If misuse/compromise is indicated, disable/reset the account, revoke sessions and tokens, and remove any attacker persistence (rules/delegations).
Scope the exposure using INV-03 and the Purview record: what data, to whom, over which channel.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Complete data-loss / breach notification as required; reinforce DLP enforcement (block vs audit) on regulated-data policies; user-awareness follow-up.
Refer over-matching policies to the DLP owners for tuning.

Escalation.Trigger: A regulated-data policy match with allowed egress, corroborated real data movement, a repeating pattern, or unconfirmed scope of exposure.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised business activity or a proven block confirmed in Purview; documented; no data left.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Account contained where needed; exposure scoped (data, recipient, channel); compliance notified; policy enforcement reviewed.
